extraFacts.fact: Sour gas service ratings on the Indus sour-service hammer union listings: Figure 1502 10,000 psi; Figure 1002 7,500 psi to 4" and 5,000 psi at 5" and 6"; Figure 1003 7,500 psi in 2" and 3" and 5,000 psi in 4" and 5"; Figure 1004 7,500 psi; Figure 602 6,000 psi; Figure 2202 15,000 psi, butt weld 2" to 6", is the sour-gas figure for 15,000 psi.
extraFacts.source: Indus Hydraulics Sour Gas Service Hammer Unions listings (/c/hammer-unions-sour-gas-service) and the guide /blog/hammer-union-figure-numbers (as-of 2026-10-06)

extraFacts.fact: Hammer unions of different figure numbers must never be joined. The male (thread) half of a 2" Figure 602 or Figure 1002 union will make up into the wing nut of a 2" Figure 1502, so a mismatched joint can look made up and then separate under pressure; IADC records a fatality from a 602-to-1502 mismatch and recommends teaching the differences between union types, go/no-go ring gauges, colour coding and segregated storage.
extraFacts.source: IADC Safety Alerts 06-01 'Mismatched Hammer Union Results in a Fatality' and 03-16 'Mismatched Hammer Unions Still Being Found' (iadc.org/safety-alerts)

extraFacts.fact: Accidents, including a fatality, have followed from hammering on hammer unions while the line was under pressure; bleed all pressure off a line before breaking it, and use lockout/tagout and permit-to-work on pressurised lines.

On elastomer-sealed hammer union figures the seal ring is a service item and should be replaced whenever it is cut, flattened or hardened. To order a union, give the figure, size, end connection and weld schedule, and whether the service is standard or sour.

faqs.q: What is a Figure 1002 butt weld hammer union used for?
faqs.a: A Figure 1002 butt weld hammer union is a 10,000 psi class, low-alloy steel union welded into cementing, acidizing, fracturing and choke lines. This standard service listing has Sch XXS butt weld ends from 1" to 6", and the 5" and 6" sizes are made with butt weld ends only.

faqs.q: How do I read the part number IH-HU-1002-BWXXS-STD-0300 on a Figure 1002 union?
faqs.a: IH-HU-1002-BWXXS-STD-0300 is a Figure 1002 hammer union with Sch XXS butt weld ends, standard service trim, 3" nominal size. The last four digits are the size: 0100 is 1", 0400 is 4" and 0600 is 6". The size table lists every part number with its weight, dimensions and rating.

faqs.q: What is the working pressure of a Figure 1002 butt weld hammer union by size?
faqs.a: The Figure 1002 butt weld union is rated 10,000 psi (690 bar) cold working pressure from 1" to 4" and 7,500 psi (517 bar) at 5" and 6". The 10,000 psi sizes are tested at 15,000 psi. Read the rating for your size in the table, not from the figure number, as our hammer union figure numbers guide explains.

faqs.q: What sizes does the Figure 1002 butt weld hammer union come in?
faqs.a: The Figure 1002 butt weld union is listed in 1", 2", 3", 4", 5" and 6", all with Sch XXS weld ends. For line pipe threaded ends, the [Figure 1002 threaded hammer union](/p/hammer-union-set-1002-series-npt-npt-10-000-psi-standard-service) covers 1" to 4"; the 5" and 6" sizes are butt weld only.

faqs.q: Should I choose a 5" or 6" Figure 1002 or a Figure 1004 for a large high-pressure line?
faqs.a: Choose the Figure 1004 if you need 10,000 psi at 5" or 6", because the 5" and 6" Figure 1002 is rated 7,500 psi and seals on an O-ring. The [Figure 1004 butt weld union](/p/hammer-union-set-1004-series-butt-weld-schedule-xxh-10-000-psi-standard-service) uses a lip-type seal instead, which avoids the O-ring union's need to be made up perfectly square.

faqs.q: What seal and material does the Figure 1002 butt weld hammer union use?
faqs.a: The Figure 1002 is made from low-alloy steel and seals on a replaceable elastomer seal ring: lip type from 1" to 4", O-ring at 5" and 6". The seal is made by the seat and ring, not the thread, so a leaking union usually needs a new seal ring or sub rather than a whole union.

faqs.q: Can a standard service Figure 1002 butt weld union be used for sour gas (H2S)?
faqs.a: No, use the sour gas trim for H2S service: the standard service Figure 1002 is not the sour version. Our sour Figure 1002 butt weld listing is rated 7,500 psi to 4" and 5,000 psi at 5" and 6", below the standard trim. See the sour gas service hammer unions shelf.

faqs.q: Which unions will mate with a Figure 1002 butt weld hammer union?
faqs.a: A Figure 1002 mates only with another Figure 1002 of the same size, from us or another maker of the figure. Never join it to a different figure: industry safety alerts record that a 2" Figure 1002 male half will make up into a 2" Figure 1502 wing nut and can separate at pressure.

faqs.q: How is a Figure 1002 butt weld hammer union made up and serviced?
faqs.a: A Figure 1002 is made up by striking the wing nut lugs with a hammer until the male and female subs seat on the seal ring. Bleed the line to zero before breaking it out, never hammer on a pressurised union, and replace the seal ring whenever it is cut, flattened or hardened.

faqs.q: What is the difference between Figure 1002 and Figure 1502 hammer unions?
faqs.a: Figure 1002 is a 10,000 psi class union and Figure 1502 is a 15,000 psi union; they are different figures and must never be connected to each other. Both are used on cementing, acidizing, fracturing and choke lines. For 15,000 psi butt weld service see the [Figure 1502 butt weld union](/p/hammer-union-set-1502-series-butt-weld-butt-weld-15-000-psi-standard-service).

faqs.q: What documents should I ask for with a Figure 1002 butt weld hammer union?
faqs.a: Ask for the material test report for the low-alloy steel subs and nut and the hydrostatic test record, which for the 10,000 psi sizes is 15,000 psi. The figure number is an industry series rather than a published standard, so state the figure, size, Sch XXS weld end and service class on the order.

faqs.q: What is a Figure 1003 misaligning hammer union used for?
faqs.a: A Figure 1003 is a misaligning hammer union that joins high-pressure water, oil, mud or gas lines where the pipe ends will not line up. It takes up to 7.5° off the centre line (15° included) and its O-ring holds pressure at any position within that allowance.

faqs.q: What does the part number IH-HU-1003-THD-STD-0300 mean?
faqs.a: IH-HU-1003-THD-STD-0300 is a 3" Figure 1003 misaligning union with line pipe threaded ends in standard service trim. THD means threaded, BWXXS means Sch XXS butt weld, and the final digits give the size, so IH-HU-1003-BWXXS-STD-0500 is the 5" butt weld union.

faqs.q: What is the pressure rating of a Figure 1003 hammer union?
faqs.a: Our standard service Figure 1003 is rated 10,000 psi (690 bar) cold working pressure in 2" and 3" and 7,500 psi (517 bar) in 4" and 5". Makers do not agree on this figure and some rate it lower, so work to the rating stamped on the union you have.

faqs.q: What sizes and end connections does the Figure 1003 misaligning union come in?
faqs.a: The Figure 1003 is listed in 2", 3", 4" and 5", with line pipe threaded ends from 2" to 4" and Sch XXS butt weld ends from 2" to 5". The 5" size is butt weld only. Weights and dimensions for each part number are in the size table.

faqs.q: How much misalignment does a 2" Figure 1003 union take compared with larger sizes?
faqs.a: The 2" Figure 1003 takes 3.5° off the centre line (7° included), half the 7.5° (15° included) of the 3", 4" and 5" sizes. If your line is further out than that, correct the pipe rather than relying on the union.

faqs.q: How does the Figure 1003 misaligning hammer union seal?
faqs.a: The Figure 1003 seals with an O-ring over steel-to-steel seating, and the O-ring holds pressure at any angle within the misalignment allowance. It suits water, oil, mud or gas service; replace the O-ring if it is cut, flattened or hardened.

faqs.q: Is there a sour gas version of the Figure 1003 misaligning union?
faqs.a: Yes, a sour gas service Figure 1003 is listed, rated 7,500 psi in 2" and 3" and 5,000 psi in 4" and 5", below this standard service union. Do not put the standard trim on an H2S line; see the [sour gas service hammer unions](/c/hammer-unions-sour-gas-service) shelf.

faqs.q: Will a Figure 1003 misaligning union connect to a Figure 1002 or 1502?
faqs.a: No. A Figure 1003 connects only to Figure 1003 halves of the same size. Never join it to a union of a different figure number: unions of different figures can look alike and partly thread together, then separate at pressure. Check the figure and size on both halves and the nut before every make-up.

faqs.q: How do you install a Figure 1003 hammer union on misaligned pipe?
faqs.a: Fit the Figure 1003 between the two pipe ends, set the angle within its allowance, then hammer the wing nut tight with the line depressurised. The O-ring seals at any angle inside 7.5° (3.5° on 2"), so do not force the pipe past that.

faqs.q: Figure 1003 vs Figure 1002: which do I need?
faqs.a: Use the Figure 1003 when the pipe ends are out of line, and the [Figure 1002 butt weld union](/p/figure-1002-hammer-union-butt-weld-standard-service) for a straight run. Both are rated 10,000 psi in the smaller sizes, but the Figure 1003 adds misalignment capacity; the two figures do not mate with each other.

faqs.q: What certificates and test data should I request for a Figure 1003 union?
faqs.a: Request the material test report and hydrostatic test record with the quotation, and the stamped working pressure for each size, since makers rate the Figure 1003 differently. Our listing claims no third-party mark, so specify any operator requirement on the enquiry.

faqs.a: Yes. We hold Figure 1003 misaligning unions in stock at our warehouse in Dubai, UAE, and ship worldwide with the best lead times; UAE delivery is within 3 working days. Send size, end connection and quantity through [our contact page](/contact).

faqs.q: What is a Figure 1505 hammer union?
faqs.a: A Figure 1505 is a 3" hammer union rated 15,000 psi, built for fracturing service and designed to connect back to existing 3" Figure 1502 iron. A thread start marker on the nut prevents cross-threading and shortens make-up time.

faqs.q: What do the Figure 1505 part numbers IH-HU-1505-THD-STD-0300 and IH-HU-1505-BW-STD-0300 mean?
faqs.a: Both are 3" Figure 1505 unions in standard service trim: THD has line pipe threaded ends and BW has butt weld ends. The final 0300 is the 3" size, the only size this figure is made in.

faqs.q: What is the working pressure of a Figure 1505 hammer union?
faqs.a: The Figure 1505 is rated 15,000 psi (1,034 bar) cold working pressure and tested at 22,500 psi in standard service. The [hammer union figure numbers guide](/blog/hammer-union-figure-numbers) sets this against the other figures from 500 to 20,000 psi.

faqs.q: What sizes does the Figure 1505 hammer union come in?
faqs.a: The Figure 1505 is made in 3" only, with a line pipe threaded or a butt weld end. No dimension table is published for it, so ask us for a dimensioned drawing if you need one before ordering.

faqs.q: When should I specify a Figure 1505 instead of a 3" Figure 1502?
faqs.a: Specify the Figure 1505 when you want a 15,000 psi 3" frac union with longer life and faster make-up that still drops into an existing 3" Figure 1502 spread. Improvements in its critical areas extend service life, and the thread start marker stops cross-threading.

faqs.q: Can the Figure 1505 hammer union be used in sour gas service?
faqs.a: A sour gas rating of 10,000 psi (690 bar), tested at 15,000 psi, is published for the Figure 1505, lower than its 15,000 psi standard rating. This listing is standard service, so state sour service on your enquiry and we will confirm the trim.

faqs.q: What service and media is the Figure 1505 hammer union intended for?
faqs.a: The Figure 1505 is intended for fracturing service at up to 15,000 psi. For cementing, acidizing and choke lines at the same class the general-purpose figure is the [Figure 1502 butt weld union](/p/hammer-union-set-1502-series-butt-weld-butt-weld-15-000-psi-standard-service).

faqs.q: Is the Figure 1505 compatible with 3" Figure 1502 hammer unions?
faqs.a: Yes. The Figure 1505 is backward connectable with 3" Figure 1502 iron, so it goes into an existing spread without changing the rest of the line. That compatibility is a stated design feature; do not assume it for any other figure or size.

faqs.q: How does the thread start marker on a Figure 1505 union help make-up?
faqs.a: The thread start marker on the Figure 1505 nut shows where to engage the thread, which removes cross-threading and cuts make-up time. Make up and break out only with the line bled to zero; never hammer on a pressurised union.

faqs.q: Figure 1505 vs Figure 2002: which is right for high-pressure frac iron?
faqs.a: Choose by pressure: the Figure 1505 is 15,000 psi in 3" only, while the [Figure 2002 hammer union](/p/figure-2002-hammer-union-butt-weld-standard-service-20000-psi) is 20,000 psi with butt weld ends from 2" to 6". The two figures do not interconnect.

faqs.q: What test documentation should I request for a Figure 1505 hammer union?
faqs.a: Request the hydrostatic test record (22,500 psi for standard service), the material test report and a dimensioned drawing, as no dimension table is published for this figure. Name standard or sour service on the order.

faqs.q: Do you keep 3" Figure 1505 hammer unions in stock?
faqs.a: Yes. We keep the 3" Figure 1505 in stock at our warehouse in Dubai, UAE, and ship worldwide with the best lead times. UAE deliveries arrive within 3 working days; send end connection and quantity through [our contact page](/contact) for a quote.

faqs.q: What is a Figure 200 butt weld hammer union used for?
faqs.a: A Figure 200 butt weld hammer union is a compact all-steel 2,000 psi union for line connections and manifolds. This listing has Sch 40 or Sch 80 butt weld ends from 2" to 8" and seals metal-to-metal on a ball and cone seat.

faqs.q: What does IH-HU-200-BW80-STD-0400 mean on a Figure 200 union?
faqs.a: IH-HU-200-BW80-STD-0400 is a 4" Figure 200 hammer union with Sch 80 butt weld ends in standard service. BW40 means Sch 40 weld ends, BW80 Sch 80, and the last four digits are the size, from 0200 (2") to 0800 (8").

faqs.q: What pressure is a Figure 200 butt weld hammer union rated for?
faqs.a: The Figure 200 butt weld union is rated 2,000 psi (138 bar) cold working pressure in every size from 2" to 8", and tested at 3,000 psi. The figure number tracks the rating, as our [hammer union figure numbers guide](/blog/hammer-union-figure-numbers) explains.

faqs.q: What sizes and weld schedules are available for the Figure 200 butt weld union?
faqs.a: The Figure 200 butt weld union comes in 2", 3", 4", 5", 6" and 8", each with Sch 40 or Sch 80 weld ends. For line pipe threaded ends from 1" up, see the [Figure 200 threaded union](/p/hammer-union-set-200-series-npt-npt-2-000-psi-standard-service).

faqs.q: Should I order Sch 40 or Sch 80 weld ends on a Figure 200 hammer union?
faqs.a: Order the weld schedule that matches the pipe you are welding to: Sch 40 for standard-wall pipe and Sch 80 for extra-strong pipe. The rating is 2,000 psi either way, but the Sch 80 union is slightly heavier and longer in each size.

faqs.q: What material and seal does the Figure 200 butt weld union use?
faqs.a: The Figure 200 is all steel and seals metal-to-metal on a ball and cone seat, with no elastomer. If you want an elastomer secondary seal behind the metal seat, the [Figure 206 butt weld union](/p/figure-206-hammer-union-butt-weld-ends-2000-psi) adds one with the same dimensions.

faqs.q: Can a Figure 200 hammer union be used on sour gas lines?
faqs.a: No sour gas rating is published for the Figure 200, so do not use it on H2S service without confirming with us first. Sour-rated figures (602, 1002, 1003, 1004, 1502 and 2202) are on the sour gas service hammer unions shelf.

faqs.q: Does the Figure 200 butt weld union mate with Figure 206 and Figure 207?
faqs.a: Yes. The Figure 206 is dimensionally identical to the Figure 200 range, and the Figure 207 blanking cap is interchangeable with both. Do not join a Figure 200 to any other figure, such as a 400 or 602.

faqs.q: How should a Figure 200 butt weld union be welded and made up?
faqs.a: Weld the Figure 200 subs to pipe of the matching schedule, then make up by hammering the wing nut until the ball and cone seats pull together. Inspect the seat for scoring before each make-up; a scored seat leaks before the thread is at fault.

faqs.q: Figure 200 vs Figure 206 hammer union: what is the difference?
faqs.a: The Figure 206 is a Figure 200 with an added secondary seal behind the metal-to-metal ball and cone seat; dimensions, weights and the 2,000 psi rating are the same. Choose the 206 where you want the extra seal.

faqs.q: What test pressure and records apply to a Figure 200 butt weld union?
faqs.a: The Figure 200 is tested at 3,000 psi against its 2,000 psi rating. Ask for the hydrostatic test record and material test report on the enquiry; the listing claims no third-party mark, so name any operator specification you work to.

faqs.q: Are Figure 200 butt weld hammer unions available ex-stock in the UAE?
faqs.a: Yes. Figure 200 butt weld unions are kept in stock at our warehouse in Dubai, UAE, and shipped worldwide with the best lead times; UAE orders arrive within 3 working days. Send sizes, schedule and quantities through [our contact page](/contact).

faqs.q: What is a Figure 2002 hammer union used for?
faqs.a: A Figure 2002 hammer union is a 20,000 psi butt weld union, the highest-rated union in our standard service range, used on 20,000 psi lines. It is made with butt weld ends only, from 2" to 6".

faqs.q: What does the Figure 2002 part number IH-HU-2002-BW-STD-0400 mean?
faqs.a: IH-HU-2002-BW-STD-0400 is a 4" Figure 2002 hammer union with butt weld ends in standard service. The final digits are the nominal size, from 0200 (2") to 0600 (6"). Check that size against the weld prep bore in the table, as some makers name sizes differently.

faqs.q: What is the pressure rating of a Figure 2002 hammer union?
faqs.a: The Figure 2002 is rated 20,000 psi (1,380 bar) cold working pressure in standard service, in every listed size from 2" to 6". Compare it with the other figures in our [hammer union figure numbers guide](/blog/hammer-union-figure-numbers).

faqs.q: What sizes does the Figure 2002 hammer union come in?
faqs.a: The Figure 2002 is listed in 2", 3", 4", 5" and 6", butt weld only. The size table gives weld prep inside and outside diameters for each size, from 31.75 mm ID on the 2" to 127 mm ID on the 6".

faqs.q: Why is a 3" Figure 2002 sometimes called 2.5" by other makers?
faqs.a: Some other makers call our 3" and 4" Figure 2002 sizes 2.5" and 3". Before ordering, match the bore of your pipe to the weld prep dimensions in the size table rather than relying on the nominal size.

faqs.q: How does the Figure 2002 hammer union seal at 20,000 psi?
faqs.a: The Figure 2002 seals with a lip-type elastomer seal backed by an anti-extrusion ring, which stops the seal being forced into the gap at 20,000 psi. Replace the seal whenever it is cut, flattened or hardened.

faqs.q: Can the Figure 2002 hammer union be used in sour gas service?
faqs.a: No separate sour gas rating is published for the Figure 2002, so this union is for standard service. For sour gas at 15,000 psi the listed figure is the Figure 2202, butt weld from 2" to 6"; see the [sour gas service hammer unions](/c/hammer-unions-sour-gas-service) shelf.

faqs.q: Which unions mate with a Figure 2002 hammer union?
faqs.a: A Figure 2002 mates only with Figure 2002 halves of the same size and bore. Never join it to a union of a different figure number: unions of different figures can look alike and partly thread together, then separate at pressure. Check figure and size on both halves and the nut before make-up.

faqs.q: What should be checked before making up a Figure 2002 union?
faqs.a: Before making up a Figure 2002, check the figure and size on both halves, the lip seal and anti-extrusion ring for damage, and that the line is bled to zero. Never hammer on a union under pressure.

faqs.q: Figure 1502 vs Figure 2002: what is the difference?
faqs.a: The Figure 2002 is rated 20,000 psi and the [Figure 1502 butt weld union](/p/hammer-union-set-1502-series-butt-weld-butt-weld-15-000-psi-standard-service) 15,000 psi; the 2002 adds an anti-extrusion ring behind its lip seal. They are different figures and must never be joined to each other.

faqs.q: What certificates should I request for a Figure 2002 hammer union?
faqs.a: Request the material test report and the hydrostatic test record for each Figure 2002, and confirm the weld prep bore against your pipe. The listing claims no third-party mark, so state any operator requirement on your enquiry.

faqs.q: What is a Figure 206 butt weld hammer union?
faqs.a: A Figure 206 butt weld hammer union is a 2,000 psi Figure 200 with a secondary seal added behind its metal-to-metal ball and cone seat, for line connections and manifolds. This listing has Sch 40 or Sch 80 weld ends from 2" to 8".

faqs.q: How is the Figure 206 part number IH-HU-206-BW40-STD-0600 decoded?
faqs.a: IH-HU-206-BW40-STD-0600 is a 6" Figure 206 union with Sch 40 butt weld ends, standard service. BW80 in place of BW40 means Sch 80 ends, and the last four digits run from 0200 (2") to 0800 (8").

faqs.q: What pressure is the Figure 206 butt weld union rated to?
faqs.a: The Figure 206 butt weld union is rated 2,000 psi (138 bar) cold working pressure in all sizes and tested at 3,000 psi. Adding the secondary seal does not change the rating of the Figure 200 it is based on.

faqs.q: What sizes does the Figure 206 butt weld hammer union come in?
faqs.a: The Figure 206 butt weld union is listed in 2", 3", 4", 5", 6" and 8", in Sch 40 or Sch 80. For line pipe threaded ends, which start at 1", see the [Figure 206 threaded union](/p/hammer-union-set-206-series-with-o-ring-metal-sub-npt-npt-2-000-psi-standard-service).

faqs.q: How do I choose between Sch 40 and Sch 80 weld ends on a Figure 206?
faqs.a: Match the Figure 206 weld end to the pipe schedule you are welding to. Both schedules carry the same 2,000 psi rating; the Sch 80 union is a little longer, for example 126.4 mm against 122.4 mm (dimension B) at 4".

faqs.q: What sealing does the Figure 206 hammer union use?
faqs.a: The Figure 206 seals metal-to-metal on a ball and cone seat, supplemented by a secondary seal. The secondary seal is there for lines where a backup is wanted behind the metal seat; inspect and replace it if it is cut or hardened.

faqs.q: Is the Figure 206 hammer union suitable for sour gas service?
faqs.a: No sour gas rating is published for the Figure 206, so treat it as standard service only. For H2S lines use a sour-rated figure from the [sour gas service hammer unions](/c/hammer-unions-sour-gas-service) shelf, or ask us to confirm a trim.

faqs.q: Will a Figure 206 mate with a Figure 200 or Figure 207 hammer union?
faqs.a: Yes. Every Figure 206 dimension matches the Figure 200 range, and the [Figure 207 blanking cap](/p/hammer-union-set-207-series-with-tappable-end-cap-2-000-psi-standard-service) is interchangeable with both. Do not join a Figure 206 to a 400, 602 or other figure.

faqs.q: How is a Figure 206 butt weld union made up in the field?
faqs.a: Weld each Figure 206 sub to matching-schedule pipe, seat the ball and cone with the secondary seal in place, and hammer the wing nut tight. Break it out only after the line is bled to zero.

faqs.q: Figure 206 vs Figure 207: what is the difference?
faqs.a: A Figure 206 is a union that joins two pipe ends, while the Figure 207 is a blanking cap that closes off the end of a line. Both are 2,000 psi and interchangeable with the Figure 200 range.

faqs.q: What test records come with a Figure 206 butt weld hammer union?
faqs.a: Ask for the 3,000 psi hydrostatic test record and the material test report when you enquire about the Figure 206. The listing makes no third-party certification claim, so state any operator specification on the order.

faqs.q: Can I order Figure 206 butt weld unions from stock in Dubai?
faqs.a: Yes. Figure 206 butt weld unions are held in stock at our warehouse in Dubai, UAE, and we ship worldwide with the best lead times; UAE delivery is within 3 working days. Send sizes and schedule through [our contact page](/contact).

faqs.q: What is a Figure 300 flat-face O-ring hammer union used for?
faqs.a: A Figure 300 is a 2,000 psi flat-face O-ring hammer union that lets a short rigid pipe section be broken out sideways. It seals equally well in low and high pressure vapour or liquid service.

faqs.q: What does the part number IH-HU-300-THD-STD-0200 mean?
faqs.a: IH-HU-300-THD-STD-0200 is a 2" Figure 300 flat-face O-ring union with line pipe threaded ends, standard service. The 1" version is IH-HU-300-THD-STD-0100; those are the two listed sizes.

faqs.q: What is the working pressure of a Figure 300 hammer union?
faqs.a: The Figure 300 is rated 2,000 psi (138 bar) cold working pressure in 1" and 2", and tested at 3,000 psi. The figure number does not track pressure here; our [hammer union figure numbers guide](/blog/hammer-union-figure-numbers) covers the exceptions.

faqs.q: What sizes does the Figure 300 hammer union come in?
faqs.a: The Figure 300 is listed in 1" and 2" with line pipe threaded ends. No dimension table is published for this figure, so ask us for a dimensioned drawing before ordering if space is tight.

faqs.q: When should I use a Figure 300 flat-face union instead of a ball and cone union?
faqs.a: Use the Figure 300 when a short rigid pipe run has to come out sideways: the flat faces part laterally, where a ball and cone seat such as the [Figure 200 threaded union](/p/hammer-union-set-200-series-npt-npt-2-000-psi-standard-service) needs axial movement to separate.

faqs.q: How does the Figure 300 seal, and in which media?
faqs.a: The Figure 300 seals on a flat-face O-ring, which holds equally in low and high pressure vapour or liquid service. Replace the O-ring whenever it is cut, flattened or hardened.

faqs.q: Is the Figure 300 hammer union rated for sour gas service?
faqs.a: No sour gas rating is published for the Figure 300, so do not use it on H2S lines without confirming with us. Sour-rated figures are on the sour gas service hammer unions shelf.

faqs.q: Which unions connect to a Figure 300 flat-face hammer union?
faqs.a: A Figure 300 connects only to Figure 300 halves of the same size. Never join it to a union of a different figure number: unions of different figures can look alike and partly thread together, then separate at pressure.

faqs.q: How do you break out a Figure 300 union on a short pipe section?
faqs.a: Bleed the line to zero, hammer the Figure 300 wing nut loose, then slide the short pipe section out sideways between the flat faces. Check the O-ring before remaking the joint.

faqs.q: Figure 300 vs Figure 211: which 2,000 psi union do I need?
faqs.a: Choose the Figure 300 for sideways breakout of short pipe runs and the [Figure 211 insulated union](/p/hammer-union-set-211-series-npt-npt-2-000-psi-standard-service) to break static or electrolytic corrosion paths. Both are 2,000 psi threaded unions but do not interconnect.

faqs.q: What documents should I ask for with a Figure 300 hammer union?
faqs.a: Ask for the 3,000 psi hydrostatic test record, the material test report and a dimensioned drawing, since no dimension table is published for the Figure 300. The listing makes no third-party certification claim.

faqs.q: Do you have Figure 300 hammer unions in stock?
